To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ouabain, an Na+, K+ ATPase blocker, completely inhibited tension development induced by Mn2+, a Ca2+ mimetic, in isotonic, K‐depolarized, Na+‐saturated medium.
ouabain, an inhibitor of cell membrane Na+,K+‐ATPases, inhibits the contractions induced by Mn2+, in the presence of glucose in the isotonic solutions with 10 mm K+ but not in 60 mm K+ solutions.
the inhibition of Mn2+‐stimulated contractions by ouabain is dependent on the decrease in the external Na+ concentrations in the K+‐depolorized taenia coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ouabian, an inhibitor of the Na+, K+ pump, on the contraction induced by manganese ion in the absence of Ca2+ in the guinea‐pigs taenia coli.
the effects of external Na+ on Mn2+‐stimulated contractions in K+ depolarized taenia.
the role of external Na+, which is the driving force for glucose transport, in the mechanism of Mn2+‐dependent contraction in Ca2+ ‐free, isotonic, K+-depolarized taenias of the guinea-pig.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contraction stimulated by Mn2+, which is dependent on external Na+, is maintained by glucose transport, which is dependent on the external Na+ gradient across cell membranes.
the contraction of the taenia coli in response to Mn2+ is maintained by Na+‐dependent glucose transport in the presence of Na+ and is independent of Na+ in its absence.
the Mn2+‐mediated contractions are maintained by Na+ transport depending on the Na+ concentration in the external medium in Ca2+ ‐free, isotonic, K‐depolarized guinea‐pig, taenia coli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Mn2+‐stimulated contraction was dependent on external Na+ in the case of K+‐depotarized taenia coli, and that the contraction induced by 5 mM Mn2+ was independent of external Na+ when the Na+ gradient was abolished by the increase in external K+, which decreased external Na+, in Ca2+−free, isotonic medium.
the Na+, K+ pump is not directly involved in the contractile mechanism of Mn2+‐stimulated taenia coli.

the contraction induced by the Mn2+ is mediated by the glucose transport depending on the Na+‐gradient in the Na+‐sufficent, K+‐depolaized taenia coli, while the contraction induced by it is mediated by the Na+‐independent glucose transport in the Na+ deficient, K+ medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of ouabains on the contraction induced by 5 mM Mn2+ in K+‐depolarized, Ca2+‐deficient taenia coli were dependent on the concentration of external K+ in the medium, and that the contraction induced by the Mn2+ was maintained by glucose uptake, which depended on external Na+, when the external Na+ concentration was sufficient.
the contraction of the taenia coli induced by Mn2+, in the presence of Ca2+‐deficient and isotonic K+ medium, is dependent on external Na+.
the Na+ gradient is an important factor in Mn2+ induced contraction in K+‐depolarized, Ca2+‐deficient taenia coli.
